about: Papers, datasets and code relevant to this repository, with what each means for our plan. Same entries as docs/logs/2026-10-07-literature.md.

entries.title: Ink Detection from Surface Topography of the Herculaneum Papyri
entries.relevance: Fine surface relief carries ink signal only near 1 um; transfer between papyri is uneven. Temper expectations for a 1 um teacher (training idea 2).

entries.title: Complete virtual unwrapping and reading of a rolled Herculaneum papyrus
entries.relevance: PHerc. 1667 read with a fragment-trained model, five rounds of scroll-specific pseudo-labelling, 1.1 um region scans and hand-corrected meshes. Supports Phase 2 (hand-fixing) and suggests a possible fourth training idea (self-training on a target).

entries.title: Model carbonized papyrus scrolls with leaded ink (XRF and CT)
entries.relevance: Ink recipe matters: leaded ink would show as density in raw CT. XRF screening proposed to prioritize scrolls.

entries.title: Virtually Unrolling the Herculaneum Papyri by Diffeomorphic Spiral Fitting
entries.relevance: The method behind villa's spiral fits and the atlas meshes; known to wander between windings in compressed regions.

entries.title: Volumetric Texture Analysis for Unsupervised Ink Detection in Herculaneum Papyri
entries.relevance: Model-free reader with no training-scroll bias; a possible second opinion on unseen scrolls. Untested at 9 um.

entries.title: Vesuvius Challenge Surface Detection (Kaggle)
entries.relevance: nnU-Net ensembles, skeleton-recall loss, Frangi post-processing: the lineage of the team's surface model.

entries.title: Volumetric Fast Fourier Convolution for Detecting Ink on the Carbonized Herculaneum Papyri
entries.relevance: Earlier ink architecture; context.

entries.title: EduceLab-Scrolls: Verifiable Recovery of Text from Herculaneum Papyri using X-ray CT
entries.relevance: The aligned fragment dataset behind supervised ink detection.

entries.title: PHerc. 172 (Scroll 5) ink labels and transcriptions
entries.relevance: Possible extra labelled scroll for training ideas 1 and 2; check resolution and segments first.

entries.title: Deciphering scrolls with tomography: A training experiment
entries.relevance: Educational; not useful here.

entries.title: Enhanced X-ray-phase-contrast-tomography brings new clarity to the 2000-year-old 'voice' of Epicurean philosopher Philodemus
entries.relevance: Early XPCT work; background.

entries.title: From invisibility to readability: Recovering the ink of Herculaneum
entries.relevance: Laboratory micro-CT can carry a carbon-ink signal. Shown on controlled samples and one opened fragment (PHerc. Paris 2 fr. 96), not on a sealed roll.

entries.title: Revealing letters in rolled Herculaneum papyri by X-ray phase-contrast imaging
entries.relevance: Synchrotron phase contrast, short letter stretches inside rolled papyrus, manual segmentation, authors list the limits. Not an absorption-CT result.

entries.title: Virtual unrolling and deciphering of Herculaneum papyri by X-ray phase-contrast tomography
entries.relevance: Longer Greek stretches from phase-contrast tomography. Parker 2019 notes these claims had not then become complete passages.

entries.title: Revealing metallic ink in Herculaneum papyri
entries.relevance: Chemistry on two opened Paris fragments. Does not show that a named sealed roll is leaded.

entries.title: Tracking ink composition on Herculaneum papyrus scrolls
entries.relevance: Lead speciation on the same kind of opened fragment. Not a CT reading.

entries.title: Shortwave-infrared imaging of text on the back of an unrolled Herculaneum papyrus
entries.relevance: Opened, mounted PHerc. 1691/1021. Needs the fragment. Not CT.

entries.title: Pulsed thermographic analysis of Herculaneum papyri
entries.relevance: Flash thermography of supported opened fragments. Needs a new physical scan.

entries.title: From damage to discovery via virtual unwrapping: Reading the scroll from En-Gedi
entries.relevance: Charred parchment with metal ink, not Herculaneum papyrus. Bright voxels do not transfer to carbon-only ink.

entries.title: Vesuvius Challenge 2023 Grand Prize: PHerc.Paris. 4
entries.relevance: Papyrologist-reviewed text from a sealed carbonized papyrus, machine learning on X-ray CT. About 5 percent of that scroll. Checked 2026-10-11.

entries.title: PHerc. 1667 read from phase-contrast CT
entries.relevance: Organizers report a papyrologist-reviewed transcription of one scroll. Hundreds remain sealed. Checked 2026-10-11.

not_found: A paper scoring v8in, d9v2 or Reader v2 on labelled held-out segments
Self-supervised pre-training for papyrus CT (only medical-CT analogues)
A Zenodo record of a 9 um ink model
